content.when_used: Estimate inventory when physical count not feasible (interim periods, casualty loss, verify physical count)

two_main_methods.gross_profit_method: Estimates COGS using historical gross profit percentage
two_main_methods.retail_inventory_method: Converts retail value to cost using cost-to-retail ratio

formula_steps: 1. Sales × Historical gross profit % = Estimated gross profit
2. Sales - Estimated gross profit = Estimated COGS
3. Beginning inventory + Purchases - Estimated COGS = Estimated ending inventory
gross_profit_method.alternative_formula: Ending inventory = Beginning inventory + Purchases - (Sales × Cost %)
gross_profit_method.not_acceptable_for: Annual financial statements (GAAP requires actual count)

gross_profit_calculation_example.facts: Beginning inventory $100K, Purchases $500K, Sales $700K. Historical gross profit % is 40%.

retail_inventory_method.concept: Retailers track inventory at retail prices (easier). Convert to cost using cost-to-retail ratio.
basic_steps: 1. Calculate goods available for sale at both COST and RETAIL
3. Calculate ending inventory at retail (GAFS at retail - Sales)
4. Convert to cost: Ending inventory at retail × Cost-to-retail ratio

conventional_retail.description: Approximates lower of cost or market (LCM)
conventional_retail.ratio_calculation: Include markups in denominator, EXCLUDE markdowns from denominator
conventional_retail.conservative: Results in lower inventory value (more conservative)

cost_method.ratio_calculation: Include BOTH markups AND markdowns in denominator
cost_method.matches_fifo_or_avg: Similar to FIFO or average cost

lifo_retail.complex: More complex, uses retail LIFO layers

retail_method_terms.markup_cancellation: Decrease in previously recorded markup (but not below original retail)

conventional_retail_example.facts: Beginning inventory: Cost $40K, Retail $60K. Purchases: Cost $200K, Retail $300K. Markups $20K, Markdown $10K. Sales $280K.
conventional_retail_example.note: Markdowns included in calculating ending inventory at retail, but excluded from ratio calculation (conventional method)

cost_method_retail_example.note: Cost method includes markdowns in ratio, results in higher inventory value

casualty_loss.use_gross_profit: Estimate inventory destroyed using gross profit method
casualty_loss.insurance_recovery: Compare estimated inventory to insurance proceeds. Loss = Inventory - Insurance recovery.
casualty_loss.example: Inventory destroyed by fire. Estimate inventory was $200K. Insurance pays $150K. Loss = $50K.

dollar_value_lifo_retail.combination: Combines dollar-value LIFO with retail method
dollar_value_lifo_retail.complexity: Advanced topic, uses price indexes and retail layers

freight_in.gross_profit_method: Add to purchases in cost calculation
freight_in.retail_method: Add to cost of goods available (cost side only, not retail side)

normal_shortage.treatment: Reduce sales (or increase COGS) before calculating ending inventory

cpa_exam_tips: Gross profit method: Ending Inv = Beg Inv + Purchases - (Sales × Cost %)
Retail method: Calculate cost-to-retail ratio, apply to ending inventory at retail
Conventional retail: Exclude markdowns from ratio (more conservative, approximates LCM)
Cost method retail: Include markdowns in ratio (approximates cost)
Gross profit method NOT acceptable for year-end GAAP statements (need actual count)
Freight-in: Add to cost of purchases

retail_method_approach: 1. Calculate GAFS at cost and retail
2. Calculate ratio (watch for conventional vs cost method)
3. Ending Inv at retail = GAFS retail - Sales (- markdowns if not already included)
4. Ending Inv at cost = Ending retail × Ratio
cpa_exam_strategies.conventional_vs_cost: Conventional = Exclude markdowns from ratio. Cost = Include markdowns in ratio.
common_mistakes: Using gross profit % instead of cost % in gross profit method
Including markdowns in conventional retail ratio (should exclude)
Forgetting to subtract sales to get ending inventory at retail

key_points: Gross profit method: Ending Inv = Beg + Purchases - (Sales × Cost %). Cost % = 100% - GP%.
Retail method: Calculate cost-to-retail ratio, apply to ending inventory at retail
Conventional retail: Exclude markdowns from ratio (approximates LCM)
Cost method retail: Include markdowns in ratio (approximates cost)
Gross profit method: Interim use OK, not acceptable for year-end GAAP
Casualty loss: Use gross profit method to estimate destroyed inventory
